subject: accordion
pitch:
Category: Object.
Subject: piano accordion.
Style: Italian mother-of-pearl.
reasoning:
I'm planning a static piano accordion model with a reasonably efficient module structure, thinking through its real-world proportions and how to orient it—bellows along one axis, standing upright with the keyboard and bass sides defined in 3D space.

I'll settle on treble box at +X so it reads on the viewer's right, with bass box at -X and bellows filling the gap between them, all standing with height along Y and keyboard facing +Z. I'm working out the dimensions: 0.40 height, 0.20 depth, treble box spanning roughly x 0.12-0.30, bass box x -0.30 to -0.12, and bellows built from 14 stacked pleated plates alternating width to create the accordion fold look.

For materials I'm planning a mother-of-pearl celluloid covering—pearly white with iridescent flecks of pale pink, aqua, and lavender—applied to the body panels. The case rests flat on the floor with the bottom at y=0, and I'm now laying out the treble keyboard face with white piano keys arranged along the front.

Working out keyboard dimensions...

I'll place black keys toward the bellows side with a pearl/gold-trimmed rail framing them. For the treble box, I'm adding a decorative decal on the top face with an SVG filigree grille design near the front.

Then I'll build out the bass box's +Z face with a 6x8 grid of small cylindrical buttons in pearl white and black, plus register switches on the treble top near the keyboard, and finish with bellows made of 15 folds.

I'm adding a leather bellows strap and a gold buckle latch at the front, plus hand straps on the bass box and simple catmull-loop shoulder straps connecting the boxes at the back. I'll also include pearl-tile decals on the box ends, top rail trim, and gold/chrome corner pieces.

For edges I'm using thin rods via a boxEdges helper to outline each box's 12 edges. I'm adding a dark backing plate beneath the treble keys with black felt rail margins, plus an "ITALIA" medallion decal facing outward on the bass box end cap.

Writing pearl mosaic shader...

I should add subtle lilac noise for iridescence. I'm settling on imports from the builder library—createBuilder, paint, patches, mix, smoothstep, noise, svg, rng—while skipping the glow kit to avoid risk. Since this is a static model with no joints, I'll use plain part placement and rod connections for structure, and I still need to work out textures like the grille filigree, medallion, and a "ROSSINI" brand plate.

I'm deciding to place the brand plate above the bass box buttons rather than on the crowded treble front, and planning out texture sprites for the grille, medallion, brand, and register labels, plus a red-and-gold striped bellows paint with grain detail. Setting up box dimensions...

Still writing bellows fold geometry...

Now I'm laying out the keyboard: a dark keybed box, then 21 white keys spaced evenly across the width with a black key pattern interspersed, positioned on the front face.

Still placing geometry...

Still setting grille orientation and placement...

For the treble end cap, I'm planning a medallion panel on the +X face of the box, positioning a plane slightly outside the cap surface with tall proportions to suggest a grille detail there.

Now I'm shifting to register switches on the top cap -- laying out six small lozenge-shaped buttons in a row near the front edge, spaced evenly along x, while shrinking and repositioning the grille so it doesn't overlap them. Then I'm moving on to the bass box, thinking through a grid of buttons across its +Z face organized in columns and rows.

Placing bass buttons...

Now adding a brand decal and corner medallion to the bass cap, gold edge trim rods at the vertical corners of both bodies with corner spheres, and sketching a leather hand strap swept along a curved path on the bass back face.

Still defining strap geometry...

Placing the strap at y=0.372 keeps it clear of the button rows and top cap, spanning from x=-0.30 to -0.02 with a gold buckle, positioned just above the bellows peaks in depth. Now I'm moving on to building the grille SVG texture.

Writing SVG code...

Then for the medallion on the bass end face, I'm planning a 100x200 oval design with "Italia" text, a star, and ornamental flourishes, sized to fit the .15x.30 plane oriented on the -X face.

I'm adding a brand plate design (120x40) with "ROSSINI" in black serif lettering surrounded by leaf flourishes, defining a gold/black/red/leather color palette, and duplicating the medallion for the treble end's grille. I'm also setting up a box helper function and configuring button cylinders with proper axis orientation, considering adding gold rim caps.

For the buttons themselves, I'm giving them a pearl-colored base with dark center dots at specific marker positions, determined by row index. I'm making sure the bass cap sits flush at y=0 so the instrument's lowest point touches the floor, then writing out all the geometry.
